items.item: Five layers used at least three different definitions of a high-confidence pick
items.detail: The hub graded 25 picks high at >=65% probability inside the band; 22 of those 25 are below 70%. The verified desk used 72% (or a 70% band selection), the board labelled 42 picks high, and the slate marked rows high at a price-only band (one ATP pick at 64.97% was labelled high). This consolidation applies one rule - >=70% AND fair decimal 1.40-101.00 - and produces 15 high picks. Every other pick is medium or low with the reason on the row.

items.item: 765 layer rows collapse to 322 fixtures; 208 fixtures appear in two or more layers
items.detail: 208 of the 322 fixtures were captured by more than one session. The same game can carry different model probabilities because each layer ran its own model. Example: Minnesota Wild at Calgary is 70.84% on the verified row but 67.38% on the hub row; Boston v Nashville is 63.69% on the board row and 66.01% on the hub row. One row per fixture is kept, the layer used is recorded in provenance, and the other layers are not blended into the number.

items.item: Inherited golf row named a tournament that finished on 4 October
items.detail: The hub and verified layers carried 'Bank of Utah Championship' on 2026-10-22. The official PGA Tour tournament page for 22-25 October 2026 is the Butterfield Bermuda Championship at Port Royal Golf Club, Southampton. The row was replaced with the official event and left unlined because strokes-gained inputs are not server-rendered. The original stale value is preserved in the hub layer.

items.item: Earlier 'Bunting withdrew' finding was not applied
items.detail: A previous session logged that Stephen Bunting withdrew from the European Championship and was replaced by Ritchie Edhouse. No official page read in this pass confirms that, Edhouse did not qualify through the European Tour Order of Merit, and multiple dated listings for 19-22 October still show Noppert v Bunting. The pair is therefore left unchanged; the PDC article could not be read past its consent wall, so the draw remains inherited rather than re-verified.

items.item: Fils ranking in the inherited write-up did not match the official capture
items.detail: The slate write-up quoted Arthur Fils at #22 with 2,050 points. The hub, slate and verified inputs all carry the 2026-10-19 ATP list at #10 with 3,325 points, and Mannarino at #79 with 743. The published write-up uses the captured #10 / 3,325 figures.

items.item: Boston write-up quoted a player total the official game page contradicts
items.detail: The board/forward text said David Pastrnak had 4 goals and 8 assists. The NHL GameCenter page for Nashville at Boston on 22 October lists Pastrnak with 6 points. The published write-up now uses the verified 6 points and Swayman's 6-1-1 / 1.98 / .928 line.

items.item: Josi assist total corrected from 8 to 6
items.detail: The Washington write-up said Roman Josi had eight assists. The official game page read today lists six assists, four goals for Ryan O'Reilly and three wins for Juuse Saros. The published text uses those figures.

items.item: Synthetic 'book' prices dropped from the slate layer
items.detail: The slate rows publish book_dec/book_am columns generated by applying a 4.5% overround to the layer's own fair price. They are not observed bookmaker prices. They were removed from the consolidated dataset; no bookmaker or tipster price is published anywhere on this desk.

Unlined by sport: cricket 1, darts 2, esports 8, gaelic-football 5, golf 2, greyhounds 13, motor-racing 1, rugby-league 3, snooker 2, tennis 3, volleyball 3. Each row states its reason (client-rendered rankings, no pre-match scoring table, futures without rosters, or a sample too small to price). No value was estimated to fill a blank.

items.item: 206 of 322 rows do not link to an individual fixture page
items.detail: 116 rows cite a URL that identifies the fixture; 193 cite a competition, rankings or tournament page and 13 cite a player page. Two tennis rows (atp-902103 and atp-902133) link to player profiles because the layer did not capture a tournament-specific schedule URL; both are flagged rather than presented as fixture-level proof.

items.item: 16 of 30 facts in the write-ups were not re-read today
items.detail: Each fact carries its source URL and an 'inherited' badge. Re-read today: NHL standings and skater leaders, the Nashville-Boston game page, the SHL table, the PGA Tour tournament page. Not re-read: LNR, URC, ATP rankings table, EHF, EuroLeague/EuroCup, NBA, MLB, Formula 1, SuperLega, PlusLiga, AFLW, NRL, LoL, GAA, GBGB.

items.item: 3 fixtures had already started before the 08:22 UTC snapshot
items.detail: New Zealand v India (07:00 UTC), plus two tennis ties at 08:00 UTC, are shown with a 'started' label and dimmed styling. They are retained for audit and are never counted as upcoming tips.

items.item: Two tri-series cricket rows cite non-fixture ICC pages
items.detail: icc-tri-m4 links to an ICC news article and icc-tri-m5 to the ICC ODI team rankings page. Neither page identifies the fixture by date and teams. The rows are retained with the exact source that was captured and are marked competition-scope on the table.

items.item: The hub layer still publishes the stale golf row and 65%-high labels
items.detail: This session's scope is the consolidated /final/ layer. The hub, verified, board, slate and forward layers are left byte-identical to their owning sessions. The defects fixed here therefore still exist in those archives; the consolidated table and its flagged page are the corrected view.

items.item: 0 rows from the ten excluded categories survived
items.detail: Soccer/football, boxing, UFC/MMA, American football, hurling, horse racing, cycling and specials are filtered by slug and asserted in tests. Gaelic football is in scope because the brief lists 'football' and 'American football' separately and does not name Gaelic football; that interpretation is documented.

items.item: 8 eSports pairings came from Liquipedia, not an official league page
items.detail: The slate layer captured the LoL Worlds 2026 Swiss Round 1 pairings from Liquipedia, a community wiki. That is not an official source, so the eight rows are published as unlined and unverified, with the official lolesports.com Worlds schedule as the outbound link. No market or pick is shown for them. This is why eSports carries eight rows but zero originated picks.

items.item: PDC article cannot be read past the consent wall
items.detail: The official PDC schedule article returns cookie-consent text in every chunk read. The darts fixtures are therefore inherited from the hub capture, with the PDC URL kept on every row.
